mike: quick heads-up — ran the new kernel-selection patch with replay harness, and the p95 for short seq (32) jumped ~18% compared to master. not consistent across runs.
sylvia: hmm. which kernel path? the heuristic that picks fp16-vnni vs int8-simd? :face_with_monocle:
mike: yes, the fallback logic that chooses 'vect_q8' for small batches. suspecting a cache-miss pattern in our matmul kernel selection. saw higher memcpy time in the profile.
anya: can you paste the flamegraph? even a tiny memcopy change can amplify at 1k rps.
mike: attaching a tiny excerpt:
```
# perf top sample (aggregated)
memcpy_avx2  34.2%
matmul_q8    28.1%
attention    12.4%
kv_cache     8.9%
other        16.4%
```
ryan: also check batching heuristics — did the harness keep client-side batching disabled? sometimes replay sets batch size to 1 and client coalescing kicks in.
mike: it was replayed with recorded interarrival times (replay-harness v2). we did synthetic with constant rps too — both show the bump but timing differs.
sylvia: could be connection priming. I remember a case where TLS session resumption was being skipped intermittently because the client reused sockets before handshake cache warmed.
anya: client details? HTTP/1.1 keepalive or gRPC? and are we using HTTP pool size defaults?
mike: gRPC over TLS, go-client default pooling (DialContext + WithMaxConns?), we used a custom pool at loadgen to mimic prod. but I noticed a flurry of `TLS handshake` events in the edge nodes logs during the high p95 window.
ryan: that matches Nagle + TLS interaction I've seen. small requests buffered then TLS records flush together -> stalls. try disabling Nagle (TCP_NODELAY) in the client and repeat.
anya: also set minimal keepalive idle to 15s in loadgen to see effect. sample curl-ish snippet for keepalive headers (for REST tests):
```
# enable keepalive on linux client socket via curl config (example)
--keepalive-time 15
# or in Go:
Transport{DisableKeepAlives: false, DialContext: (&net.Dialer{KeepAlive: 15 * time.Second}).DialContext}
```
sylvia: FYI we have an existing test that compared gRPC vs REST but didn't control for connection churn. results were misleading: REST looked faster because our REST loadgen used keepalives and gRPC didn't reuse streams properly.
mike: exactly — apples-to-apples is hard. we need a test matrix that locks: keepalive behavior, pool size, concurrency, TLS session reuse, and same payloads. otherwise kernel/quantization differences get blamed.
ryan: for KV cache behavior, I noticed that our in-memory KV shadow has a cold-start penalty: first 1000 requests incur lock contention on the cache init. Could explain early-run regressions.
anya: add a warmup phase in harness: 5k multi-threaded warmup requests distributed across model shards. that should prime KV and jitted kernels.
dev-bot: deploy-bot: replay-harness v2 started on infra-staging @ 1767777020 :rocket:
mike: did a quick experiment: 1) disable socket reuse in client -> p95 drops 12% but CPU up 4%. 2) set TCP_NODELAY -> p95 drops 9%. 3) larger batch window (50ms) -> different kernel chosen and p95 improved for long-seq but regressed for short-seq.
sylvia: helps to add a deterministic selector in kernel selection during benching: force kernel X for baseline runs, then force kernel Y. that isolates kernel perf from batching artifacts.
yan: also capture per-request model path metadata (kernel name, quantization, batch-size) in trace logs. then we can group latencies by kernel choice.
anya: we've been bitten by clock skew between loadgen VMs — I recommend using monotonic timers for interarrival replay and record server-side arrival timestamps for correlation.
mike: action items:
- add warmup phase to replay harness (anya)
- instrument traces with kernel/kv metadata (ryan)
- run controlled A/B where client keepalive and TCP_NODELAY toggled (sylvia)
- produce flamegraphs for both synthetic and replay runs and diff them (mike)
- short note in the benchmark playbook about apples-to-apples variables (all)
sylvia: I'll also check whether the kernel-selector heuristic has a bias threshold that flips on small-batch variance. might add hysteresis.
anya: one more: if TLS handshake spikes, capture `ss -tanp` snapshot and `openssl s_client -showcerts` logs — sometimes cert chain validation delays appear on some nodes.
mike: thanks all. I'll run 3 controlled comparisons tonight and post summaries. please flag if you want different knobs toggled.
ryan: please include raw p50/p95/p99 + QPS curves and also the connection churn timeline. even a 2s spike with 100 handshakes can skew p99.
anya: :thumbsup: good plan.
mike: posting results in this thread tomorrow.
